Welcome to Victoria Drive Primary PRU.
Victoria Drive PRU is a safe place that aims to make a difference to any pupil who is currently finding school challenging. We approach these challenges in a creative, flexible and innovative way that is bespoke to each individual child.
We value the honest relationships that we build with our parents and make every effort to build trust in order to ensure the best outcomes for our pupils and their families.
Eileen Shannon Head Teacher
Our Vision
Restore
Rebuild
Return
Leaders provide a positive, nurturing and well-organised environment...
“Leaders provide a positive, nurturing and well-organised environment. The curriculum helps pupils learn how to work and play alongside others. Pupils develop strategies to regulate their behaviour independently during the short time that they spend here.
Leaders have developed a positive and respectful school culture that is shared by all.”
Pupils who attend the school are happy and safe...
“Pupils who attend the school are happy and safe. They enjoy their lessons and like the clear routines that the school provides. Leaders have high expectations that pupils should work hard, do their best and behave well. Pupils respond to these expectations very positively.”
Pupils take part in range of activities, including cultural visits and local trips...
“Pupils take part in range of activities, including cultural visits and local trips. These are carefully planned to enhance pupils’ experiences as part of the wider curriculum. Leaders’ work to promote pupils’ interests and talents is excellent. Pupils achieve exceptionally well.”
The school is a highly calm and orderly place to learn...
“The school is a highly calm and orderly place to learn. If a pupil does get upset, adults help them to become ready to learn again as soon as possible. Pupils who are anti-bullying ambassadors support others in understanding and preventing bullying. Leaders deal with any incidents quickly and effectively.”

Vision
Restore confidence, trust and readiness to learn.
Rebuild skills, resilience and relationships.
Return to mainstream stronger and equipped to thrive.
Ethos
At Victoria Drive, we believe every child deserves the chance to restore, rebuild and return. We are committed to providing a safe, nurturing and therapeutic learning environment where pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs are supported to re-engage with education and achieve positive outcomes. Our practice is rooted in nurture principles, strong relationships and a clear understanding that behaviour is a form of communication.
Staff provide consistent, structured and compassionate support to help pupils develop emotional regulation, resilience and the confidence needed to succeed in school and beyond. We have high academic and personal expectations for every pupil. Teaching and learning opportunities are carefully adapted to meet individual needs, enabling pupils to make progress from their starting points and to prepare successfully for reintegration into mainstream education or the next stage of their learning. Pupils’ voices are central to our work. We act as advocates for every child, ensuring they feel heard, valued and respected. Through positive role modelling, restorative approaches and therapeutic support, we help pupils develop the skills they need to build healthy relationships and make safe, responsible choices.
Play, creativity and structured therapeutic activities are used to support engagement, promote wellbeing and develop independence. We work closely with families, schools and external professionals to provide a joined-up, holistic approach that supports both learning and emotional development. Safeguarding is at the heart of everything we do. Victoria Drive provides a calm, predictable and supportive environment where pupils feel secure enough to take risks, experience success and believe in their future. Victoria Drive is a place where we make a difference, every day, for every child.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us - Victoria Drive Primary Pupil Referral Unit
pageCache.text:
About Us
A key strand of the policy and practice of behaviour management at Victoria Drive PRU is to work collaboratively with Wandsworth primary school practitioners to support pupils with SEMH to access education and become happy learners.
Staff in schools are encouraged to use the PRU’s ethos to understand and respond to pupils’ SEMH needs. This involves a close partnership and a Team Around the Child (TAC) approach. This Service also offers full time education to any pupil who is a Wandsworth resident and has been permanently excluded from their primary school. Pupils referred to this Service can: receive specialist teaching and support either at the PRU or in their own school, to enable them to develop strategies for managing their behaviour to enable them to access learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: PSHE/RSE - Victoria Drive Primary Pupil Referral Unit
pageCache.text:
PSHE/RSE
PHSE lessons help pupils to develop their knowledge and skills to be able to keep themselves safe and healthy and to make informed decisions.
PSHE is embedded throughout the curriculum with an aim to develop resilience, self-esteem, collaboration, respect and positive emotional health, reduce barriers to learning, raise aspirations and improve the life chances for pupils with Social, Emotional and Mental Health Difficulties through our PSHE curriculum and quality first teaching.
Children show how they are feeling by using the zones of regulation display during their sessions. This helps staff understand a child’s emotional state and open dialogue for SEMH.
Within our PSHE curriculum, we have included the statutory guidance for:
At Victoria Drive, the overall success of the PSHE curriculum is measured using the ‘Boxall Profile’, whereby pupil’s Social, Emotional and Mental Health Development (SEMH) is assessed by their school at the beginning of their time at Victoria Drive PRU and then re-assessed throughout. This measure becomes a bespoke SEMH target setting strategy for each pupil. Individual targets are then reviewed by the network supporting this pupil. Each pupil also has an Individual Care Plan which shares key information about the pupil’s triggers, behaviours, and supportive factors so all adults can maximise positive interactions.

Wellbeing Champions
In every group, we nominate a Wellbeing Champion during our Class meeting. This pupil could have shown; kindness; focused learning; great team work; resilience; compassion and support for others to name but a few. What is inspiring and motivating is that the pupil is nominated by the previous winner and they share the reason(s) for the nomination. The Wellbeing Bear is then presented to the pupil for the rest of the day and it is always gratefully received. The pupils are thoughtful when it is their turn to nominate, proud to share compliments at the same time as practising small group public speaking.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Nurture Approach - Victoria Drive Primary Pupil Referral Unit
pageCache.text:
Our Nurture Approach
We believe that children learn best when they feel safe, understood and supported, and that strong relationships are the foundation for success in school.
Our nurture provision is a very important part of what makes Victoria Drive unique.We provide a calm, caring environment that feels welcoming and secure, with spaces designed to support both learning and emotional development. Our classroom includes a comfortable living-room style area alongside a learning space, and we use both throughout the day so that children can learn in a way that feels safe and natural for them.
We place a strong focus on helping children to understand their feelings and behaviour.
Through daily conversations, play, social activities and restorative approaches, pupils are supported to talk about emotions, build positive relationships and learn how to manage challenges.
Through our nurture approach, every child has their own individual targets, known as Boxall SEMH targets, which help us plan the right support for them. Activities are carefully chosen to match each child’s needs, strengths and stage of development. We understand that some children need a different approach to learning, and nurture allows us to provide this in a structured, consistent and thoughtful way.

This helps children to feel more confident, develop emotional regulation, and become ready to learn again.
At Victoria Drive, nurture is not just a room —it is a way of working that helps children feel valued, build trust and believe that they can succeed.

Educational Outings
Reading
A love of reading is encouraged in all our work. We use The Five Minute Box multi-sensory programmes to develop children’s phonics and high frequency word reading skills, and every pupil reads a book matched to their reading level with an adult in every session. This helps develop children’s confidence in reading aloud, enhances their comprehension skills and extends their vocabulary knowledge. Pupils also have a guided reading session each week in order to be led through a variety of fiction and non-fiction texts. Each day, children also get access to Reading Eggs online. Designed by literacy experts, Reading Eggs makes learning essential reading and phonics skills easy and fun. The program uses a highly motivating sequence of online reading lessons, activities and books.
We also love story time at Victoria Drive PRU. The children love being read to in our nurturing reading corners. Pupil voice is important in generating a reading for pleasure culture, therefore the children take part in daily book vote as part of the reading process.
“Leaders ensure that there is a strong culture of reading. Right from the start, staff check pupils’ reading abilities and interests. For pupils who are at the early stages of reading, teachers provide high levels of support. Extra phonics and reading sessions help pupils who fall behind to catch up successfully. Pupils develop a love of reading. Staff encourage pupils to read widely. Pupils enjoy reading high-quality texts that help develop their vocabulary.”
Writing
We follow the Pie Corbett Talk for Writing approach, where children learn a text through regular repetition before developing it into a piece of their own writing. Teacher modelling of writing is used to show pupils the skills and processes essential to effective writing, and key vocabulary for a topic is shared and displayed so that the pupils have the tools to hand to be successful and confident writers. Movement and oracy is a key part of writing curriculum and encourages the children to re-develop a love for writing and being proud of what they can achieve.
Oracy
Through all our work we give children time to think, speak and listen to one another. We model clear Standard English and support pupils to phrase and re-phrase their thoughts and views and to present their ideas fluently using an increasingly wide vocabulary. We use a wide variety of strategies to give every child a voice, and in our weekly class meetings children think and talk together about local, national and global issues. Developing and practising these skills in our small group setting enables children to build the confidence to have their voices heard at school and in the wider world.

​Overview
At Victoria Drive PRU, we teach maths (number) during every session. Our lessons are reated from assessments completed by the children’s mainstream schools. From the completed assessments we create lessons which provide challenge for the children while also providing the opportunity to learn new skills and acquire knowledge. In Victoria Drive PRU our focus is on the teaching number (place, value, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and fractions). Lessons are delivered on a rolling basis.
Approach
At Victoria Drive PRU, we employ the maths mastery approach using the CPA (Concrete, pictorial, abstract) approach across both Key Stage 1 and 2. The mastery approach scaffolds our pupils learning to move from concrete maths (using materials) to pictorial (pictures) and then onto abstract including solving abstract problems. We use White Rose maths to support and inform our maths mastery steps. CPA is detailed below.
Concrete step of CPA
Pictorial Step of CPA
Abstract step of CPA
Abstract is the “symbolic” stage, where children use abstract symbols to model problems. Students will not progress to this stage until they have demonstrated that they have solid understanding of the concrete and pictorial stages of the problem. The abstract stage involves the teacher introducing abstract concepts (for example, mathematical symbols). Children are introduced to the concept at a symbolic level, using only numbers, notion, and mathematical symbols (for example, +, -, x,/) to indicate addition, multiplication or division.
Maths Environment
In Victoria Drive PRU, we utilise both the indoor and outdoor spaces to help to relate mathematical concepts to the world around them. Our personalised maths lessons aim to deepen children’s understanding, build fluency, accelerate progress, and support children to find the most efficient ways of calculating and solving maths challenges.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding at Victoria Drive Pupil Referral Unit runs throughout everything that we do. The premises are secure and safe; resources are stored safely, and pupils are taught to use them responsibly. Our robust PSHE curriculum helps our pupils to make safe choices in school and as citizens in the wider community.

We guide our practice using relevant, current legislation, including Keeping Children Safe in Education 2025, Working Together to Safeguard Children 2018 and the Children Act 1989.

Open Playground has been a huge success at Victoria Drive PRU.
There has been a lot of interest from Wandsworth schools and numbers of attendance has been growing since our first session in April 26. We currently have 18 children attending with their TA and 3 staff members of staff from Victoria Drive. The structured play activities allow the children to engage and explore in a range of play activities, encouraging them to be independent learners and to take risks. If children show a theme of play that they enjoy and engage in then this will be noted and planned for the following week.
The children are encouraged to direct their own play and communicate how they want to extend and develop the activity further. The adults interact and use this time to network and share good practice. The Open Playground community is a warm, friendly and nurturing space for all who attend. We enjoy being around each other and use this time to build on our own experiences and share good practise.

pageCache.pageTitle: Research Projects - Victoria Drive Primary Pupil Referral Unit
pageCache.text:
Research Projects
By participating in research projects, reviewing current evidence and evaluating the impact of interventions, staff are able to reflect on and refine their practice, ensuring that support for pupils is informed by the latest developments in education, psychology and wellbeing. Research also promotes a culture of curiosity, collaboration and professional growth, encouraging staff to explore innovative approaches and share learning with colleagues and partner schools. Ultimately, this leads to improved outcomes for pupils, as staff are better equipped to meet their individual needs and provide high-quality, evidence-informed provision. Psychologist and Educational Specialists can also learn from the approached we use at the PRU to support children with their SEMH needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning Mentor - Victoria Drive Primary Pupil Referral Unit
pageCache.text:
Learning Mentor
At the beginning, a meeting takes place with the SENCo, parent or carer, child and Teacher so that we can find out how best to support the pupil. This can take place in the pupil’s school for 1 or 2 hours every week and is tailored around the pupil’s specific needs that we find out from the Boxall Profile. The support offered is reviewed regularly with the school and pupil’s family.
